body:
Good Monday morning, Bakersfield. The week opens with a milestone worth celebrating — a Mira Monte sophomore who made school history at the national FFA convention — alongside a busy night for first responders and a mild, clear fall day ahead. Expect a high near 75, light winds, and moderate air quality, with no weather alerts or active fires anywhere in Kern County.

## The Kern Overnight

The night's most serious call came early. At 1:24 a.m., officers were sent to Chester Lane on a report of an assault with a baseball bat, where a 40-year-old man was listed as a possible victim. About half an hour later, officers asked a local hospital to check whether anyone had come in with injuries from an assault with a deadly weapon — a routine step when the details of a fight are still coming together.

The biggest response of the night belonged to South Union Avenue. Just after 11:30 p.m., a caller reported hearing a gunshot and seeing three people fighting across the street, one of them in a red shirt and possibly armed. Officers set a perimeter around South Union and Serrano Drive, posting units on Acres, Millwood Court, Birchwood Court and Juniper while the air unit circled overhead. They held the block, confirmed an offense, and then searched the alley behind the fire station for shell casings.

Two weapons calls came in hours apart. At 10 p.m., officers were sent after a man who told a caller he had a firearm in his pocket and had arrived in a gray SUV. Then at 1:07 a.m., deputies went to the 8200 block of Kimber Avenue in southeast Bakersfield over reports of people with a small black handgun; a newer blue Subaru SUV left the area, and no firearm was recovered.

Before dawn, at 5:25 a.m., two callers reported a man trying to force a woman into the back seat of a car in an alley behind a residence. There was no description of the vehicle, and officers were sent back to the block. The night's heaviest fire call came at 8:57 p.m., when crews found heavy smoke pouring from a roughly 1,500-square-foot building in the 2000 block of Lake Street in east Bakersfield. The fire was reinforced and worked as a high-priority search, and one engine stayed on scene with smoke still in the attic.

## Today's weather

It's 55 degrees right now at Meadows Field, on the way to a high near 75 this afternoon and a low around 52 tonight — about as pleasant an October Monday as the valley gives us. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and there are no active fires to track. Air quality sits at 69, which the index rates as moderate; if you're sensitive to particulates, it's a reasonable day to keep an eye on how you feel during longer stretches outside. Otherwise, expect a calm, dry day with plenty of sun.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that a Bakersfield musician has built a business around a problem most players never think about.** Jim Schaffer, founder of Southpaw Soundwaves, is left-handed, and he told the station that finding a guitar that felt right was a lifelong frustration — enough of one that some left-handed players give up and learn to play right-handed instead. He didn't. Schaffer started with a ukulele kit that, by his own account, sounded terrible, built another that sounded just as bad, and eventually sought guidance from a master instrument maker in Hawaii. About 15 years ago, while teaching Exploring Technology at Earl Warren Junior High, he began having students build their own ukuleles, capped with a concert at the end of the school year.

**According to 23ABC, a Mira Monte High School sophomore has made school history at the National FFA Convention and Expo in Indianapolis.** Isaac Ovalle took first place in reciting the FFA Creed in Spanish — the first time a Mira Monte student has won the event — competing against 46 students from across the country. The format calls for reciting all five paragraphs and answering three questions within five minutes, and Ovalle said he practiced for days to memorize and polish the speech. His agriculture teacher, Crystal Luera, told the station he has come a long way since joining the chapter and called the win a point of pride for bilingual public speaking at the school.

**KGET 17 reports that a new Angel Walk is bringing hope to domestic violence survivors in Bakersfield.** The walk honors survivors and remembers those lost, giving families and advocates a public way to mark a problem that often stays behind closed doors. We'll have more detail as the event takes shape.

**KGET 17 also has Week 10 of the high school football season covered, with results and highlights from across Bakersfield and Kern County.** Late October means league races are tightening and playoff seeding is coming into view, so this week's slate carried real weight for several local teams.

**Bakersfield police are searching for a suspect in an east Bakersfield burglary, KGET 17 reports.** Investigators have not released further details, and anyone with information should contact the department directly rather than through us.

**Bakersfield Now reports that Kern County sheriff's deputies eradicated 204 marijuana plants while serving a search warrant in Taft, with one person arrested.** Illegal grows of this kind draw concerns beyond the plants themselves — water theft, unsafe electrical wiring, and environmental damage on the land — which is why the sheriff's office treats them as more than a simple drug case.

## Something good

Hundreds of families turned out Sunday for Clinica Sierra Vista's free Trunk-or-Treat in southwest Bakersfield, with a line of costumed kids stretching around the parking lot. Grandmother Jamie Lujan told 23ABC the best part was bringing the whole family without worrying about the cost. Community organizations were on hand too, connecting parents with services across Kern County — and the host was marking its 55th anniversary while handing out candy.

## Coming up this week

Halloween week is here, and the Fox Theater has the calendar covered. Tonight and tomorrow, October 26 and 27, J & J Investigations leads Ghost Tours at the Fox — a chance to walk the historic theater after dark and hear what the investigators have turned up. Friday, October 30, brings ELIAS MEDINA to the Fox stage, and if you're planning further ahead, Journey USA plays the Fox on November 7, with TEXAS TORNADO TRADITION also set for November 7. The Fox's Cults & Classics season pass for 2026–2027 is on sale now for film fans who want the whole series.

No public meetings appear on the calendar for today, so it's a quiet start to the week on the civic front — a good window to catch up before the end-of-month agendas land. If you're heading out for early trick-or-treating or a school Halloween event later this week, the weather should cooperate: mild days, cool evenings, and no rain in sight. Have a good Monday, and we'll see you back here tomorrow.

top.title: Bakersfield musician builds handcrafted guitars to give left-handed players more options
